analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts and the complete workflow patch. The change adds a workflow-wide release toolchain selector (HEAD 112–114) and changes the compatibility artifact's expected SDK from 27.0 to 27.2 (patch HEAD 1444). No supported security regression is established in these units. Source verification still precedes credential-consuming jobs (BASE .github/workflows/release-provider.yml:143–182); build and qualification use the verified source (203–207, 276–280), and signing requires successful qualification or the retained-build recovery contract (327–331). The supplied signing path retains hardened-runtime signing, entitlement checks, notarization, final archive signature verification, full CodeDirectory hashing and comparison of the executable's linked SDK with the selected build SDK (655–757, 819–838, 938–983). These controls relate to A-011/A-017, TB-003/TB-009 and T-034/T-054; the patch does not visibly weaken them or alter inference encryption, token authorization, billing or plaintext handling.
Integration must examine scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and .github/actions/provider-release-build to confirm DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release selects and enforces Xcode/SDK 27.2 consistently across build, qualification and signing, including resumed unsigned artifacts. The workflow compares BUILD_SDK_VERSION with PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION before signing (BASE 442–460), but selector semantics and recovery metadata validation are outside these excerpts. Also verify the changed compatibility assertion against its surrounding HEAD source and generated validation identity. This is a coverage limit and an unresolved cross-file contract, not evidence of a bypass.
